narrative.overview:
R-ELEC reads as a white, airy page that holds a few big rounded blocks: a full-width photo card, deep night-navy panels, soft grey panels. White carries trust. Navy and yellow carry urgency, and they always appear together, the way a lit call-out van shows up at night. The page builds its rhythm from blocks, never from rules: no grid lines, no rails, no hairline scaffolding between sections. Only a generous vertical gap (5rem, then 7rem on desktop) separates sections.

Density is low and the type is confident: semibold Onest headings with tight tracking, comfortable 1.0625rem body text, and figures set in Martian Mono so the proof (2006, 24/7, 5/5, the phone number) reads like an instrument readout. Only one element moves continuously: the yellow "line open" dot that pulses next to every emergency statement. Everything else is still at rest. It lifts or brightens on hover, and fades in once on scroll where the browser supports scroll timelines.

The brand is strict, per PRODUCT.md: blue `brand` is the identity, yellow `volt` is a rare accent, white dominates, and no other brand hue exists. Yellow never sits as text on a light ground.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, with grey `panel` and navy `navy-900` blocks as the only large surfaces.
Large rounded blocks (1.75rem), rounded cards (1.25rem), pill buttons.
Two-tone headlines: grey lead-in, brand-blue payoff on white; white text with a yellow payoff on navy.
Martian Mono 500 for display figures and large phone numbers.
Round yellow icon pastilles with navy Lucide line icons.
CSS-only motion (pulse, scroll reveal, hover lift), all of it cut under reduced motion.
A sticky two-button call bar on mobile.

rules.name: The No Yellow on White Rule
rules.body: Volt is never used as text or as a thin mark on white or panel grey. On a light ground it only appears as a filled button or pastille with navy text, and the live dot on light grounds gets a 2px navy ring.

rules.name: The Paired Urgency Rule
rules.body: Yellow appears with navy: navy text on a yellow fill, or yellow text on a navy surface. A yellow accent with no navy nearby is off-system.

rules.name: The No Third Hue Rule
rules.body: Only blue, yellow and their navy/grey derivatives are allowed. Status colours (such as the form error orange) are functional and never decorative.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Headline Rule
rules.body: Every section H2 splits into a lead-in and a payoff. On white the lead-in is `ink-soft` and the payoff is `brand`. On navy the lead-in is white and the payoff is `volt`. Only one payoff per heading.

rules.name: The Instrument Figure Rule
rules.body: Numbers that serve as proof, and phone numbers set at display size, use Martian Mono with tabular figures. Phone numbers inside buttons and running text stay in Onest with tabular-nums.

rules.name: The French Spacing Rule
rules.body: Visible copy goes through the `fr()` helper (`src/lib/typo.ts`), or uses literal ` `, so `? ! : ; »` and the opening `«` never orphan at a line break.

rules.name: The No Rails Rule
rules.body: Sections and blocks are never framed by grid lines, column rails or decorative rules. Hairlines are only allowed as functional list separators (FAQ, safety steps), field borders, and the sticky header and call-bar edges.

rules.name: The Lift on Intent Rule
rules.body: Cards rise 2px and pick up their shadow only on hover or focus. Stat tiles brighten to `navy-700` instead of moving. Photo cards scale their image 3% and turn their arrow pastille 45 degrees.

rules.name: The One Living Thing Rule
rules.body: The live dot (2.4s pulse) is the only element that animates continuously. Scroll reveals (fade, 1.5rem rise, 4px unblur) run once, need `animation-timeline: view()`, and leave content visible by default. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the pulse, reveals, smooth scroll, menu slide and FAQ height transition are all switched off.

dos: Do keep white dominant, and use `panel` and `navy-900` blocks at 1.75rem radius as the only large surfaces.
Do split every section H2 into an `ink-soft` lead-in and a `brand` payoff on white, or a white lead-in and a `volt` payoff on navy.
Do set proof figures and display-size phone numbers in Martian Mono 500 with tabular figures.
Do put the live dot in front of every 24/7 availability statement.
Do run visible French copy through `fr()` so punctuation never orphans.
Do gate every animation behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, or cancel it under `reduce`.
donts: Don't set yellow text, or a thin yellow mark, on white or panel grey.
Don't separate sections or frame blocks with grid lines, column rails or decorative rules.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker label above headings. The two-tone H2 does that job.
Don't introduce a third brand hue, or animate anything continuously other than the live dot.
Don't use square corners on buttons, cards or photos.
